/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 14 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3195 (6)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5316 (-24)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2503 (49)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1558 (5)
Baltic Handysize Index: 851 (3)
CAPESIZE
Ascension Day resulted in a quieter overall session, with the market pausing slightly following the strong gains seen earlier in the week. The BCI 182 5TC eased by $224 to close at $48,209, as sentiment across both basins became a touch more measured despite generally healthy underlying cargo volumes. In the Pacific, activity levels remained solid overall, although the tone turned slightly mixed as miner resistance became more apparent throughout the day. Two miners were initially active on C5, although one was later reported to have temporised, contributing to softer sentiment into the close. Offers on C5 began the session around the $16.00 mark before gradually slipping into the high $15s, with one miner reportedly bidding closer to $14.50. By the close, offers had moved into the low $15s, although no fixtures had been reported at the time of writing. Consequently, C5 slipped by 0.457 to $15.433. The Atlantic basin presented a similarly mixed picture. The North Atlantic remained comparatively firm, supported by stronger transatlantic activity, with a notable fixture helping push C8 up by $2,625 to $56,938. However, South Brazil and West Africa to China business softened marginally, with limited fresh activity reported on C3. Bid levels were heard around $36 against low $37s for index dates, leaving C3 marginally higher by $0.202 at $36.925.
PANAMAX
Another day of positive momentum in the Panamax market across the Atlantic basin, although overall activity was slightly subdued due to the widespread European holiday. The trans Atlantic market maintained its upward trajectory, with brokers highlighting its close correlation to the strength in the fronthaul market, alongside an increase in both mineral and grain volumes. The fronthaul sector continued to show a firm trend, with multiple fixtures reported, albeit at a slower pace compared to previous sessions. In the Pacific, sentiment appeared more mixed. Some market participants noted a remaining demand for prompt tonnage in Southeast Asia, particularly for mineral runs from Indonesia and Australia. However, others suggested the market may be pausing as charterers reassess fundamentals and pull back on bids. The Bettys Love (77,171 2008) open in Tianjin 15/17 May was reported as fixed for a trip with coal via East Coast Australia to South China with the rate discussed as between $20,500 and $22,250 to Guaransea. The Zhong Chang Zhou Shan (75,409 2013) open in Gunsan 27/30 May was reported to have been placed on subjects for period of a minimum duration of 25 October to a maximum of 25 December 2026 at $19,300, although the charterer remained unknown. The P5TC increased by $445 concluding to $22,528.
SUPRAMAX
With the widespread European holiday unsurprisingly, it was a rather slow day in the Atlantic and brokers said that fundamentals changed little in the Atlantic. Asia remained buoyant, with the north maintaining demand and some reasonable levels being discussed. The Yun Tong Hai (64,708 2025) open Caofeidian 20 May was heard fixed for a trip to West Africa at $24,500 but no more details came to light. The Sea Aquarius (53,468 2006) open Zhoushan 23/25 May was heard fixed also to West Africa in low $19,000s, again no more details were disclosed. The Astro Vega (63,008 2015) Huludao 15/18 May was heard fixed $21,500 for a trip Thailand with steel, again further details remained lacking. Period activity surfaced, the Britian Bay (58,709 2012) Mizushima 17/19 May was said to have been placed on subjects at $19,000 for 4/6 months trading. The 11TC average closed up $73 at $19,698.

HANDYSIZE
The market delivered another mixed session, with weakness in Atlantic side due to holidays offset by modest gains in Pacific. The BHSI rose 3 points to 851, while the 7TC average increased by $56 to close at $15,311. In both the Continent and Mediterranean, only minor changes were recorded, with rates easing slightly from previous levels. Meanwhile, the South Atlantic and US Gulf were notably quiet, with limited reported activity and rates beginning to soften. In contrast, Asia maintained a healthy pace of trading, with owners and charterers gradually lifting their rate ideas. A 38,000-dwt vessel open in the Philippines was fixed via West Australia to the Far East at $17,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Brazil Soybean Exports Eye New May Record

Brazil’s soybean export pace continues to strengthen, with ANEC raising its May forecast to 16.0 Mt from 14.5 Mt last week, putting shipments on track for a record May volume. The revised estimate would mark a 12.7% year-on-year increase, while cumulative soybean exports for January-May are projected at 59.1 Mt, up 8.9% from 2025 levels. Soybean meal exports are also expected to surge 35.6% year-on-year to 2.9 Mt, reflecting firm global demand. Meanwhile, May corn exports are forecast at 308,570 tonnes, well above last year’s 68,400 tonnes.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve lost value today in response to a negative index, with the Pacific drifting lower while the Atlantic market remains tight. The Jun contract was the heaviest with 37650 sold, followed by the May contract with 41750 sold. The May v Jun contract continues to widen and strengthen trading north of 4000. Jul was under pressure also with 34250 trading, while the Q3 struggled for liquidity trading within a range of 33000-33300. Q4 was relatively inactive today with a small clip done at 31850. Cal27 closed marginally weaker also, with 26650 sold.

PMX
The PMX market was quieter today, with the curve finding some support through the morning before easing back off into the close. May traded in a narrow range of 21650–21700, holding steady throughout the session. June remained the main point of interest, trading 22250–22650 and seeing the most activity, but values softened back towards the close to 22100. July bounced around 21550 and 22000. Q3 traded 20650–21000. Further out, Q4 printed 18650–18850, while Nov saw a single print at 18900. Cal 27 remained steady in a tight range of 15425–15550.

SMX + HANDY
SMX had a slower session today, with most of the activity focused around the front months. June was the standout contract, trading between 19000 and 19300, while May held at 17900. July traded in a narrower 19000–19200 range, with August moved 18550–18750 and September remaining quiet around 18100–18150. Further along the curve, Q3 printed 18400–18600, while Jun-Dec and Q3+Q4 strips traded at 17600 and 17550. Q4 moved between 16500 and 16750, with Q127 holding around 12750. On the back end, Cal 27 traded 13500–13650 and Cal 28 printed 12500–12550.

Carbon
EU carbon markets remained nearly unchanged today, as many European countries observed Ascension Day. The benchmark Dec26 contract was assessed at �75.02/eua, down �0.04, with traded volumes below10m EUAs.

Market Fundamentals
Brazil Soybean Exports Eye New May Record
Brazil’s soybean export pace continues to strengthen, with
ANEC raising its May forecast to 16.0 Mt from 14.5 Mt last
week, putting shipments on track for a record May volume.
The revised estimate would mark a 12.7% year-on-year
increase, while cumulative soybean exports for January-May
are projected at 59.1 Mt, up 8.9% from 2025 levels. Soybean
meal exports are also expected to surge 35.6% year-on-year
to 2.9 Mt, reﬂecting ﬁrm global demand. Meanwhile, May
corn exports are forecast at 308,570 tonnes, well above last
year’s 68,400 tonnes.
Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve lost value today in response to a
negative index, with the Paciﬁc drifting lower while the
Atlantic market remains tight. The Jun contract was the
heaviest with 37650 sold, followed by the May contract with
41750 sold. The May v Jun contract continues to widen and
strengthen trading north of 4000. Jul was under pressure
also with 34250 trading, while the Q3 struggled for liquidity
trading within a range of 33000-33300. Q4 was relatively
inactive today with a small clip done at 31850. Cal27 closed
marginally weaker also, with 26650 sold.
PMX
The PMX market was quieter today, with the curve ﬁnding
some support through the morning before easing back oﬀ
into the close. May traded in a narrow range of 21650–21700,
holding steady throughout the session. June remained the
main point of interest, trading 22250–22650 and seeing the
most activity, but values softened back towards the close to
22100. July bounced around 21550 and 22000. Q3 traded
20650–21000. Further out, Q4 printed 18650–18850, while
Nov saw a single print at 18900. Cal 27 remained steady in a
tight range of 15425–15550.
SMX + HANDY
SMX had a slower session today, with most of the activity
focused around the front months. June was the standout
contract, trading between 19000 and 19300, while May held
at 17900. July traded in a narrower 19000–19200 range, with
August moved 18550–18750 and September remaining quiet
around 18100–18150. Further along the curve, Q3 printed
18400–18600, while Jun-Dec and Q3+Q4 strips traded at
17600 and 17550. Q4 moved between 16500 and 16750, with
Q127 holding around 12750. On the back end, Cal 27 traded
13500–13650 and Cal 28 printed 12500–12550.Cape 180 5TC

The revised estimate would mark a 12.7% year-on-year increase, while cumulative soybean exports for January-May are projected at 59.1 Mt, up 8.9% from 2025 levels. Soybean meal exports are also expected to surge 35.6% year-on-year to 2.9 Mt, reflecting firm global demand. Meanwhile, May corn exports are forecast at 308,570 tonnes, well above last year’s 68,400 tonnes. Trading Commentary Cape The Cape FFA curve lost value today in response to a negative index, with the Pacific drifting lower while the Atlantic market remains tight. The Jun contract was the heaviest with 37650 sold, followed by the May contract with 41750 sold. The May v Jun contract continues to widen and strengthen trading north of 4000. Jul was under pressure also with 34250 trading, while the Q3 struggled for liquidity trading within a range of 33000-33300. Q4 was relatively inactive today with a small clip done at 31850. Cal27 closed marginally weaker also, with 26650 sold. PMX The PMX market was quieter today, with the curve finding some support through the morning before easing back off into the close. May traded in a narrow range of 21650–21700, holding steady throughout the session. June remained the main point of interest, trading 22250–22650 and seeing the most activity, but values softened back towards the close to 22100. July bounced around 21550 and 22000. Q3 traded 20650–21000. Further out, Q4 printed 18650–18850, while Nov saw a single print at 18900. Cal 27 remained steady in a tight range of 15425–15550. SMX + HANDY SMX had a slower session today, with most of the activity focused around the front months. June was the standout contract, trading between 19000 and 19300, while May held at 17900. July traded in a narrower 19000–19200 range, with August moved 18550–18750 and September remaining quiet around 18100–18150. Further along the curve, Q3 printed 18400–18600, while Jun-Dec and Q3+Q4 strips traded at 17600 and 17550. Q4 moved between 16500 and 16750, with Q127 holding around 12750. ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场整体趋稳，BDI小幅上扬6点至3195。capesize因太平洋市场走弱拖累指数下跌24点，但大西洋区域表现强劲；panamax持续走强，p5tc上涨445美元至22528，所有航线全面上扬；supramax和handysize温和回升。期货曲线显示capesize近月合约大幅贴水，panamax曲线趋于陡峭化。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: BDI收3195点，capesize回调24点但大西洋c8航线逆势上涨2625美元；panamax领涨各船型，p5tc劲扬445美元，大西洋与太平洋市场同步走强；supramax亚洲区域维持活跃，11tc小升73美元。整体呈现大西洋稳、太平洋分化的格局。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: capesize太平洋c5航线回落0.457至15.433，矿商压价意愿显现；panamax大西洋航线全面飘红，p1a_82跳涨941美元显示跨大西洋需求旺盛；supramax西非流向s5_63大涨332美元；期货capesize q3'26至33000-33150区域流动性不足，近月贴水加深反映短期压力。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注capesize太平洋c5与c3的价差收敛机会；panamax大西洋fronthaul与transatlantic联动走强，期现套利空间需关注；supramax亚洲西非航线s3/s5维持高位，支撑11tc合约；handysize亚洲持续活跃，7tc录得56美元涨幅。

market_watch: capesize c5太平洋航线矿商抵制压价，报价从16美元回落至15.4美元，关注是否测试14.5支撑
panamax大西洋p1a_82劲升941美元，transatlantic需求强劲或延续至端午假期后
supramax s5西非经南美东岸至中国航线涨332美元，亚洲区域内需求保持韧性

route_focus.view: tubarao至青岛航线$36.925微涨0.202美元，南美粮食出货平稳，短期支撑仍存但涨幅受限。
skaw-gibraltar大西洋往返航线$20,500跳涨941美元，领涨panamax各航线，跨大西洋需求旺盛。
handysize 38k船型菲律宾至西澳远东航线$17,000成交，亚洲市场活跃度支撑7tc上行。
